question: Which of the following food additives have nutritive value?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Nutritional Supplements__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nutritional supplements have additives and nutritive value.
 
• Nutritional supplements, in foods, any vitamin or mineral added during processing to improve nutritive value and sometimes to provide specific nutrients in which populations are deficient.
 
• Flour and bread products are often enriched with iron and the B vitamins thiamin, riboflavin, and niacin; and citrus fruit beverages, naturally containing vitamin C, may be fortified with additional vitamin C units.
 
• The addition of iodine to salt has eliminated goiter in some areas in which it was formerly common, and vitamin D may be added to baby foods to combat rickets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fat emulsifiers

 
 
• Emulsification is the process of combining two substances that normally don't mix well together.
 
• To emulsify fats usually means to mix them with water-based liquids and a binding substance like bile salts or other compounds, which has important implications for cooking and digestion.
 
• Egg yolks, which contain fat suspended in water, are both an emulsion and a highly effective emulsifier.
 
 
 
• Antioxidants
 
 
• ​Antioxidants, natural or synthetic food preservatives, are additives that preserve food.
 
• It prevents oxidative deterioration in storage and processing.
 
• Due to their high stability and low volatility, the antioxidants help to maintain the level of nutrients, texture, color, taste, freshness, functionality, aroma, and appeal to consumers such as the older person, ceteris paribus.
 
• Antioxidants are not only in food additives but are also to be found in food supplements and levels should be measured, as such, in body tissues and fluids.
 
 
 
• **Preservatives**
 
 
• Food preservatives are chemicals that are added to food to protect it from microbes that could contaminate or rot it.
 
• The most common chemicals used to inhibit the growth of microorganisms are salts and edible oils. As a result, they are referred to as preservatives.
 
• To prevent microbes from attacking pickles, we add salt or acid preservatives.
 
• These are also used to prevent spoilage in jams and squashes. 
 
• Common preservatives include sodium benzoate and sodium metabisulphite. 
 
• Sodium benzoate is used as a food preservative because of its anti-fungal properties. This chemical compound enters each cell and balances the pH of the food, effectively increasing the acidity of the food and assisting in food preservation.
 
• Many pharmaceutical formulations contain sodium metabisulphite as an antioxidant. It is widely used as a preservative and disinfectant in food.
